title: User Notifications

requirements.text: Notify users about important events so they do not miss things happening in their accounts
Notifications should be timely and not overwhelming (balance frequency to avoid spam and avoid missed events)

known_issues: Delivery channel is never specified — 'wherever makes the most sense' does not name email, push, SMS, in-app, or webhook.
'Important events' is never enumerated — no concrete event types are listed.
Frequency is described only qualitatively ('sweet spot', 'not too many/few') with no cadence, batching, or digest rule.
No definition of 'appropriately' / 'the right people ... right things ... right time' — targeting and rules are undefined.
No opt-out or preference mechanism is stated despite mentioning users 'turn them off'.
hallucination_traps: Do NOT invent specific channels (email, push, SMS, Slack) that the PRD never commits to.
Do NOT invent a specific event list (e.g. 'password changed', 'payment failed', 'new comment').
Do NOT invent a concrete frequency such as 'daily digest' or 'max 3 per day'.
Do NOT invent a preferences/settings UI or per-channel toggles as if specified.
Do NOT assume a notifications infrastructure/provider (e.g. Firebase, Twilio, SES).
notes: A faithful parser should produce a task to define notification requirements — enumerate which events trigger notifications, which channel(s) to use, and frequency/cadence rules — surfacing these as open decisions. It should NOT emit implementation tasks for a specific channel or event as though those were stated.
